l: Surah 35: The Originator (Faatir)
s: Allah is owner of praise (as the Absolute)
q: And Allah! He is the Absolute, the Owner of Praise.

l: Surah 35: The Originator (Faatir)
s: Allah is forgiving forgiveness

l: Surah 35: The Originator (Faatir)
s: Allah is observer of Allah's slaves
q: Lo! Allah is indeed Observer, Seer of His slaves.

l: Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: This unit concerns Allah's warnings, judgments, guidance, and commands to mankind, including belief in the Hour of Doom, the Resurrection, and the Day of Resurrection. It describes the consequences for the believers and the disbelievers, including entry into the Gardens or punishment in the Fire. It explains the rites of the pilgrimage, the sanctity of the Inviolable Place of Worship and the holy House, and commands regarding worship, sacrifice, and charitable giving. It also recounts opposition to Allah's messengers, the role of Satan, and Allah's defense of those who are true.

l: Allah, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: Allah is described as the Truth, Able to do all things, the Judge, the Guide, the Defender of those who are true, and the Owner of Praise. Allah gives life, causes death, raises the dead, judges between people, provides for those who flee for His cause, and commands worship, pilgrimage rites, sacrifice, and charity.

l: Muhammad, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: Muhammad is addressed as a warner, messenger, and witness. He is told to proclaim the pilgrimage, summon mankind to Allah, and say that Allah will judge between those who differ.

l: mankind, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: Mankind is warned to fear Allah and is described as created through stages, brought forth as infants, and eventually dying or reaching an abject age. Mankind includes believers, disbelievers, disputants concerning Allah, those who worship Allah conditionally, and those who will be judged on the Day of Resurrection.

l: the believers, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The believers are promised pardon, rich provision, the Gardens, armlets of gold and pearls, silk garments, gentle speech, and a good entry. They are commanded to bow, prostrate, worship Allah, do good, establish worship, pay the poor-due, and hold fast to Allah.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The disbelievers are threatened with garments of fire, boiling fluid, melted entrails and skins, hooked rods of iron, and punishment in the Fire. They deny the revelations, bar people from the way of Allah, and remain in doubt until the Hour or a disastrous day comes.

l: Satan, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: Satan proposes opposition when a messenger or prophet recites the message. Allah abolishes what Satan proposes and establishes His revelations, while Satan's proposal becomes a temptation for those whose hearts have disease or are hardened.

l: the Hour of Doom, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The Hour of Doom is described as a tremendous earthquake whose sight will make nursing mothers forget their nurslings and pregnant women deliver their burdens. It will come without doubt, and Allah will raise those in the graves.

l: the Resurrection, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The Resurrection is presented as a truth demonstrated by Allah's creation of mankind, the revival of barren earth, and Allah's power to quicken the dead. Allah will raise those who are in the graves.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will judge between people and decide among those who believe, Jews, Sabaeans, Christians, Magians, and idolaters. The believers will be in Gardens, while the disbelievers will receive a shameful doom.

l: the Doom of Allah, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The Doom of Allah will overpower mankind when the Hour is seen, making them appear drunken though they are not. It is also described as a punishment that causes fear, anguish, and burning.

l: the pilgrimage, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The pilgrimage is proclaimed to mankind, who will come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine. Its rites include witnessing benefits, mentioning Allah's name over cattle, feeding the poor, ending unkemptness, fulfilling vows, and going around the ancient House.

l: the Inviolable Place of Worship, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The Inviolable Place of Worship is described as appointed for mankind, including both its dwellers and nomads. Those who disbelieve and bar people from it, or seek wrongful partiality there, are threatened with a painful doom.

l: the holy House, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The holy House is the place whose location Allah prepared for Abraham. Allah commanded that it be kept free of partners, purified for those who go around it, stand, bow, and prostrate.

l: the ancient House, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The ancient House is the destination around which pilgrims go after completing their unkemptness and vows. Sacrificial cattle are brought to it after their appointed benefits.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The Hereafter is included in the loss of those who worship Allah only on a narrow margin and turn away when tested. Those who flee their homes for Allah's cause and are slain or die are promised provision and a welcomed entry.

l: the Fire, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The Fire is promised to those who strive to thwart Allah's revelations and to those who disbelieve. It is described as a hapless journey's end and as punishment involving burning, boiling fluid, and iron rods.

l: the Gardens, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The Gardens are promised to those who believe and do good works. Rivers flow beneath them, and their inhabitants receive armlets of gold, pearls, silk garments, gentle speech, and a good provision.

l: worship, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: Worship is established as a duty of those given power in the land, together with paying the poor-due, enjoining kindness, and forbidding iniquity. Believers are commanded to establish worship, bow, prostrate, and worship their Lord.

l: the revelations, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The revelations are described as plain and established by Allah after He abolishes what Satan proposes. The disbelievers deny them and react with hostility, while those given knowledge recognize their truth and submit humbly.

l: the believers and the disbelievers, Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj), Surah 22: The Pilgrimage (Al-Hajj)
s: The believers and the disbelievers are two opponents who contend concerning their Lord. The believers enter the Gardens, while the disbelievers receive garments of fire and other punishment.

l: Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor) concerns Allah's revelations, legal and social guidance, the conduct of believers, and warnings to those who slander or disbelieve. It addresses accusations, privacy, modesty, marriage, worship, obedience to the messenger, and relations within the community. It describes Allah's light, the signs in the heavens and the earth, and the consequences awaiting believers and disbelievers in the world and the Hereafter.

l: Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: It is a surah revealed and enjoined by Allah at Medina. It contains plain revelations and admonitions concerning belief, conduct, worship, judgment, and the consequences of deeds.

l: Allah, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: Allah reveals and explains the revelations, commands believers, forgives and shows mercy, and knows what people reveal and hide. He is described as Clement, Wise, Knower, Hearer, Merciful, the Manifest Truth, and the Light of the heavens and the earth.

l: the believers, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: The believers are instructed to obey Allah and the messenger, establish worship, pay the poor-due, guard modesty, avoid slander, seek permission, and follow Allah's guidance. Those who hear and obey are described as successful and victorious.

l: the slander, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: The slander is spread by a gang among the community and is treated as a serious matter. Those who spread it or love its spread concerning believers face punishment, while believers are admonished not to repeat it.

l: the devil, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: The devil commands filthiness and wrong through his footsteps. Believers are told not to follow those footsteps.

l: believing women, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: Believing women are instructed to lower their gaze, guard their modesty, conceal their adornment except where permitted, draw their veils over their bosoms, and avoid displaying hidden adornment. Those who traduce virtuous, believing women face a severe punishment.

l: the messenger, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: The messenger is obeyed as Allah's messenger and is charged with conveying the message plainly. Believers appeal to him for judgment, ask his leave when on a common errand, and are instructed not to treat his calling as an ordinary person's calling.

l: Allah's revelations, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: Allah's revelations are sent down, made plain, explained, and expounded for people. They provide admonition, guidance, legal instruction, and examples for those who ward off evil.

l: Allah's light, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: Allah's light is likened to a lamp in a niche, shining through glass and kindled from a blessed olive tree. Allah guides whom He wills to His light and speaks to mankind in allegories.

l: the heavens and the earth, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: The heavens and the earth belong to Allah, and all who are in them praise Him, including the birds in their flight. Allah's signs include clouds, rain, hail, lightning, the alternation of day and night, and the creation of every animal from water.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: The deeds of the disbelievers are compared to a mirage and to layers of darkness. They cannot escape in the land, and fire will be their home.

l: the straight path, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: Allah guides whom He wills unto a straight path through the revelations. Obeying Allah and the messenger leads people aright.

l: worship, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: Worship includes remembrance of Allah, constancy in prayer, praising Him morning and evening, establishing worship, and paying the poor-due. Believers are commanded to maintain it and obey the messenger.

l: the Day of Return, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: On the Day of Return, people are brought back to Allah and informed of what they did. Their tongues, hands, and feet testify against them, and Allah pays them their just due.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor), Surah 24: The Light (An-Noor)
s: The Hereafter contains an awful doom for those who commit or spread slander and for the disbelievers. Allah's grace, mercy, forgiveness, and bountiful provision are promised to those who believe, repent, and do good.

l: Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: This unit concerns Allah's revelation of the Criterion to Muhammad as a warning to the peoples and describes the objections of the disbelievers. It contrasts the fate of those who deny the Hour, reject the Qur'an, and worship other gods with the rewards promised to the righteous and the faithful slaves of the Beneficent. It recounts Allah's signs in creation, the missions of earlier messengers, and the punishment of past peoples. It also describes the qualities of Allah's faithful slaves, including humility, night worship, moderation, avoidance of falsehood, acceptance of revelations, repentance, and righteous work.

l: Allah, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: Allah reveals the Criterion to His slave, creates everything, measures it, and possesses the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth. He is Forgiving, Merciful, Powerful, and sends messengers, signs, guidance, punishment, and reward.

l: Muhammad, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: Muhammad receives the Criterion and is sent as a warner and bearer of good tidings. The disbelievers mock him, question his eating and walking in markets, and accuse him of following sorcery, while Allah strengthens his heart through revelation.

l: the Criterion, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The Criterion is revealed to Allah's slave so that he may warn the peoples. It is presented as the truth and as an argument against the similitudes brought by the disbelievers.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The disbelievers accuse Muhammad of inventing a lie, call the revelation fables, demand signs, and reject the Hour and the Qur'an. They will face the fire, hardship, and judgment.

l: other gods, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: Other gods are chosen beside Allah, but they create nothing and are themselves created. They possess no power over hurt, profit, death, life, or raising the dead.

l: the Hour, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The Hour is denied by the disbelievers, who do not look for a meeting with Allah. Those who deny its coming will face a prepared flame.

l: Hell, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: Hell is described as a place whose crackling and roaring are heard from afar. The guilty are flung into a narrow place of it, chained together, and made to wish for destruction.

l: the Garden of Immortality, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The Garden of Immortality is promised to those who ward off evil. It will be their reward and journey's end, where they abide and have all that they desire.

l: the angels, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The angels will be sent down in a grand descent when the heaven is rent asunder. On the day the guilty behold them, the angels bring no good tidings for the guilty.

l: Satan, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: Satan is described as man's deserter in the hour of need. He leads a person astray from the Reminder after it has reached him.

l: the Qur'an, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The Qur'an is accused by the disbelievers of being invented and dictated from ancient fables. It is revealed in an ordered manner to strengthen Muhammad's heart, and Muhammad's own folk make it of no account.

l: the righteous, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The righteous are promised the Garden, a better home, and a happier place of noonday rest. Those who repent, believe, and do righteous work have their evil deeds changed to good deeds.

l: the faithful slaves of the Beneficent, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The faithful slaves of the Beneficent walk modestly, answer foolish people with peace, spend nights prostrate and standing, and ask to be protected from Hell. They spend moderately, avoid major sins and vanity, accept revelations, and seek comfort in their families while becoming patterns for those who ward off evil.

l: the Sovereignty, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The Sovereignty belongs to Allah, who has no son or partner in it. On the day of judgment, the True Sovereignty belongs to the Beneficent One.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: On the Day of Resurrection, the doom is doubled for those who persist in wrongdoing and they abide disdained forever. Those who repent, believe, and do righteous work are treated with forgiveness and mercy.

l: the judgment, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The judgment concerns the denial of truth and the deeds of people. Allah will make wrongdoers taste great torment, while those who repent and do good receive forgiveness and changed deeds.

l: the doom, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The doom prepared for evil-doers is painful, and the doom of Hell is anguish. It is doubled for persistent wrongdoers on the Day of Resurrection, while the disbelievers face a hard day.

l: the resurrection, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The disbelievers hope for no resurrection and therefore pass by Allah's signs without accepting them. The resurrection is nevertheless presented as a coming reality connected with judgment and reward.

l: the warning, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The warning is delivered through Muhammad, the Criterion, the revelations, and examples of destroyed peoples. It is meant to make people remember and turn toward Allah.

l: the way, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: The way is the path toward Allah, and Muhammad invites whoever wills to choose it. Those who reject it are described as astray and farther from the right road.

l: water, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: Allah sends purifying water from the sky to give life to dead land and to provide drink for many beasts and human beings. He also sets a bar between two seas, one sweet and palatable and the other saltish and bitter.

l: human beings, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: Human beings are created from water and given kindred by blood and marriage. Many of them begrudge everything except ingratitude, while the faithful among them are tested and guided through warning.

l: the revelations, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: Allah's revelations are denied by guilty peoples and serve as reminders and warnings. The faithful do not respond to them as deaf or blind, but accept them with humility.

l: repentance, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: Repentance is accepted from the one who turns away from wrongdoing, believes, and does righteous work. Whoever repents and does good truly repents toward Allah.

l: righteous work, Surah 25: The Criterion (Al-Furqaan), 1 Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples.
s: Righteous work accompanies repentance and belief and leads to Allah's forgiveness and the transformation of evil deeds into good deeds. Those who do good are promised reward and a lasting place.

l: Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: This unit concerns Allah’s revelations, the Qur'an, and the guidance given to believers, while disbelievers reject the Hereafter and face punishment. It recounts Moses receiving signs, and Solomon ruling over people, jinn, birds, and ants before receiving the Queen of Sheba and her people’s submission to Allah. It recalls the destruction of wrongdoers among Pharaoh’s people, Thamud, and Lot’s folk, and describes Allah’s signs in the heavens and the earth. It warns of resurrection, Judgment Day, the Trumpet, the beast of the earth, and the consequences of good and evil deeds.

l: Allah, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Allah is described as the Lord of the Worlds, the Mighty, the Wise, the Forgiving, the Merciful, and the Absolute in independence. Allah gives signs, knowledge, provision, guidance, mercy, judgment, and resurrection, and nothing hidden in the heavens or the earth escapes His clear Record.

l: Muhammad, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Muhammad receives the Qur'an from the presence of One Wise, Aware. He is commanded to trust Allah, serve Him, recite the Qur'an, warn those who go astray, and proclaim Allah’s signs.

l: Moses, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Moses sees a fire, receives Allah’s call, and is given signs including his staff becoming a moving creature and his hand coming forth white but unhurt. He is sent with nine tokens to Pharaoh and his people, who call them magic and deny them.

l: Solomon, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Solomon inherits David, is taught the language of birds, and is given abundance. He commands armies, investigates the hoopoe, communicates with the Queen of Sheba, and asks Allah to make him thankful.

l: Queen of Sheba, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: The Queen of Sheba rules her people and possesses a mighty throne. She consults her chieftains, sends a present to Solomon, recognizes his letter, and ultimately says that she surrenders with Solomon unto Allah.

l: Sheba, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Sheba is the land from which the hoopoe brings Solomon sure tidings. Its people are found worshipping the sun instead of Allah and are ruled by a woman.

l: Qur'an, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: The Qur'an is described as revelations and a Scripture that makes plain, a guidance and mercy for believers. It narrates much of what the Children of Israel differ about and is to be recited by Muhammad.

l: Hereafter, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: The Hereafter is affirmed as certain, while those who do not believe in it have their works made fairseeming and become astray. The unit says that good deeds receive better than their worth and evil deeds lead to the Fire.

l: believers, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Believers establish worship, pay the poor-due, and are sure of the Hereafter. They receive guidance and mercy, and those who ward off evil are saved.

l: disbelievers, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Disbelievers reject the revelations and the Hereafter, deny resurrection, and call the promise of being raised again fables. They are described as facing the worst punishment and being among the greatest losers.

l: Solomon's armies, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Solomon's armies consist of jinn, humankind, and birds, gathered and arranged in battle order. They pass through the Valley of the Ants, where an ant warns the ants to enter their dwellings lest they be crushed unperceiving.

l: ants, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: The ants are warned by one ant to enter their dwellings so that Solomon and his armies do not crush them unperceiving. Solomon smiles at the ant’s speech and asks Allah to make him thankful.

l: Valley of the Ants, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: The Valley of the Ants is reached by Solomon and his armies. An ant there warns the other ants about the danger of being crushed.

l: Solomon's throne, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Solomon's throne is not described in this unit; the text instead describes the Queen of Sheba's mighty throne, which Solomon orders brought before him.

l: Solomon's letter, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Solomon's letter is thrown down to the Queen of Sheba's people. It identifies Solomon, begins in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful, and calls them not to exalt themselves and to come as those who surrender.

l: the beast of the earth, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: The beast of the earth will be brought forth when the word is fulfilled concerning mankind. It will speak to them because mankind did not have faith in Allah’s revelations.

l: the Trumpet, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: The Trumpet will be blown on the Day when those in the heavens and the earth will start in fear, except whom Allah wills. All will come unto Allah humbled.

l: resurrection, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Resurrection is rejected by those who ask whether they will be brought forth after becoming dust like their fathers. The unit declares that the dead will be raised and that people will be gathered before their Lord.

l: Judgment Day, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: On Judgment Day, a host from every nation who denied the revelations will be gathered and questioned. The word will be fulfilled against those who did wrong, and good and evil deeds will receive their respective consequences.

l: worship, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Worship is commanded toward Allah alone, the Lord of the Worlds and the Lord of the hallowed land. The Queen of Sheba's people are criticized for worshipping the sun instead of Allah.

l: guidance, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Guidance comes through the Qur'an, which is described as guidance and mercy for believers. Those who follow the right way benefit their own souls, while Muhammad is commanded only to warn those who go astray.

l: idolatry, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: Idolatry appears when the Queen of Sheba and her people worship the sun instead of Allah. Satan makes their works fairseeming and bars them from the way of Truth.

l: the heavens and the earth, Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml), Surah 27: The Ant (An-Naml)
s: The heavens and the earth contain Allah’s signs, including water, orchards, rivers, firm hills, the barrier between two seas, and the alternation of night and day. Allah knows the hidden and the proclaimed in them, and nothing hidden in either is absent from a clear Record.

l: Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), revealed at Mecca, concerns belief, testing, worship, and accountability before Allah. It recounts how Allah tested earlier peoples, including Noah, Abraham, Lot, Midian, A'ad, Thamud, Korah, Pharaoh, and Haman, and describes the consequences of their deeds. It teaches that believers who persevere, trust Allah, and do good works will receive mercy and dwell in the Garden, while disbelievers and wrong-doers face Allah's doom. It urges mankind to worship Allah alone, remember Him, seek provision from Him, and follow His guidance.

l: Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: This unit was revealed at Mecca and teaches that belief is tested, Allah knows the sincere and the hypocrites, and every soul will return to Him for judgment. It recounts examples involving Noah, Abraham, Lot, and earlier peoples, and compares those who choose patrons besides Allah to a spider building a frail house.

l: Allah, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Allah tests people, knows what is in their hearts, forgives evil deeds, guides those who strive in Him, provides for His creatures, and is independent of them. He creates and recreates, punishes and shows mercy, rescues whom He wills, and will judge all people.

l: mankind, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Mankind is commanded to worship Allah, show kindness to parents, seek provision from Allah, and travel the land to observe how creation began. Some of mankind believe sincerely, while others are hypocritical, deny the revelations, or invent lies concerning Allah.

l: believers, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Believers are tested, but Allah knows those who are sincere. Those who believe, do good works, persevere, and trust their Lord will have their evil deeds remitted and will enter among the righteous and dwell securely in the Garden.

l: disbelievers, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Disbelievers deny Allah's revelations, reject the meeting with Him, and urge believers to follow their way while falsely promising to bear their sins. They will face Allah's doom and have no hope of His mercy.

l: Noah, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Noah was sent as a messenger to his folk and remained with them for a thousand years save fifty years before the flood engulfed the wrong-doers. Allah rescued Noah and those with him in the ship and made it a sign for the peoples.

l: Abraham, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Abraham called his folk to serve Allah and keep their duty to Him, warning them that idols provide no provision. His folk answered by proposing to kill or burn him, but Allah saved him from the Fire, bestowed Isaac and Jacob on him, established prophethood and Scripture among his seed, and gave him reward in the world and righteousness in the Hereafter.

l: Lot, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Lot believed Abraham and said he was a fugitive unto his Lord. He condemned his folk's lewdness and corruption, and Allah's messengers delivered Lot and his household from the destruction of the township, except his wife, who stayed behind.

l: idols, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Idols are served instead of Allah, but they own no provision for those who serve them. Abraham said that the love connected with them belongs only to the life of the world, and that on the Day of Resurrection their followers will deny and curse one another.

l: the Scripture, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: The Scripture was revealed to Muhammad and is read to the people as mercy and a reminder for those who believe. It is also described as clear revelations in the hearts of those given knowledge, and the People of the Scripture are told to believe in what was revealed to both communities.

l: Allah's revelations, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Allah's revelations are denied by disbelievers and wrong-doers, while those given knowledge recognize them. The text says that none deny Allah's revelations save disbelievers or wrong-doers.

l: worship, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Worship is commanded as service to Allah alone. Establishing worship preserves people from lewdness and iniquity, though remembrance of Allah is described as more important.

l: the meeting with Allah, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: The meeting with Allah is certain, and whoever looks forward to it should know that Allah's reckoning is near. Those who disbelieve in the meeting with Him have no hope of His mercy and face a painful doom.

l: testing with affliction, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: People who say they believe are tested with affliction. Some mistake persecution by mankind for Allah's punishment, but Allah knows the believers and the hypocrites.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: On the Day of Resurrection, those who followed idols will deny and curse one another, and they will have no helpers. People will also be questioned about the loads and inventions they carried in the world.

l: death, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Every soul will taste of death, and afterward all will be returned to Allah.

l: the Fire, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: The Fire is the abode promised to those who choose idols, and it will be the dwelling of the disbelievers. Allah saved Abraham from it when his folk sought to burn him.

l: Allah's doom, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Allah's doom is not to be hastened, because its appointed term is fixed, but it will come suddenly upon those who deny. It will overwhelm the disbelievers from above and beneath their feet, and they will be told to taste what they used to do.

l: creation and recreation, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Allah produces creation and then reproduces it, and this is easy for Him. People are urged to travel in the land and see how He originated creation and brings forth later growth.

l: provision, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Allah alone provides for creatures, including animals that do not carry their own provision. He widens provision for whom He wills and straitens it for whom He wills, and idols possess no provision for those who serve them.

l: the heavens and the earth, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth, and their creation is a sign for believers. He constrained the sun and the moon to their appointed work, and even those questioned about their creator acknowledge that Allah created them.

l: the spider's house, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: The spider's house is used as a likeness for those who choose patrons besides Allah. It is described as the frailest of all houses, if people only knew.

l: remembrance of Allah, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Remembrance of Allah is more important than the preserving effect of worship. Allah knows what people do while they worship and remember Him.

l: guidance, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Allah guides those who strive in Him to His paths. Satan made the deeds of A'ad and Thamud seem fair to them and thereby debarred them from the Way, despite their keen observation.

l: good works, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Those who believe and do good works will have their evil deeds remitted and will be admitted among the righteous. They will be housed in lofty dwellings of the Garden beneath which rivers flow.

l: sin, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: Disbelievers cannot bear the sins of those they mislead, although they claim they will do so. They will bear their own loads and other loads beside their own, and will be questioned about what they invented.

l: the world, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: The love between idolaters is limited to the life of the world, and the world is described as pastime and a game. The home of the Hereafter is the true Life, if people only knew.

l: the Garden, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: The Garden is promised to believers who do good works, persevere, and trust their Lord. They will dwell securely in lofty dwellings beneath which rivers flow.

l: the Last Day's judgment, Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot), Surah 29: The Spider (Al-Ankaboot)
s: The Last Day's judgment includes questioning people about their invented claims and deeds. On that day idolaters will deny and curse one another, while the disbelievers will face the Fire and have no helpers.

l: Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: The unit concerns Allah's power over creation, resurrection, provision, mercy, and judgment, and His signs in the heavens, the earth, and human life. It recounts that the Romans will recover after defeat, while believers will rejoice in Allah's help to victory and disbelievers will face consequences. Mankind is urged to follow the upright religion, give charity, avoid usury and partners ascribed to Allah, and reflect on Allah's revelations and signs. The Hour and the Day of Resurrection will separate people, rewarding believers who do good and bringing disbelievers and wrongdoers to doom.

l: Allah, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Allah creates, sustains, causes to die, gives life, guides, judges, and has power over the heavens and the earth. He is Mighty, Merciful, Wise, and does not fail in His promise.

l: Muhammad, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Muhammad is instructed to call people to the upright religion, patience, worship, duty to Allah, and reflection on His signs. He is told that he cannot make the dead hear or guide the blind from error, but can make believers hear Allah's revelations.

l: The Romans, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: The Romans have been defeated in the nearer land, but after their defeat they will be victorious within ten years. Believers will rejoice in Allah's help to victory on that day.

l: believers, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Believers rejoice in Allah's help to victory and are rewarded for believing and doing good works. They will be made happy in a Garden.

l: disbelievers, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Disbelievers deny Allah's revelations and the meeting of the Hereafter, and they will be brought to doom. Allah does not love those who disbelieve in His guidance.

l: mankind, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Mankind is urged to ponder, travel through the land, reflect on Allah's signs, follow the upright religion, give due to relatives and the needy, and avoid associating partners with Allah. Most of mankind do not know, are heedless of the Hereafter, or disbelieve in meeting their Lord.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: The Hereafter is neglected by those who know only the outward appearance of worldly life. Those who deny the meeting of the Hereafter will be brought to doom.

l: the heavens, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: The heavens were created by Allah and stand fast by His command. They belong to Him, and His signs include their creation and their relation to rain, lightning, and the resurrection.

l: the earth, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: The earth was created with truth and a destined end, and Allah revives it after its death. Corruption appears on land because of what people's hands have done, and Allah's signs are seen in the earth's revival.

l: the Garden, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: The Garden is where those who believed and did good works will be made happy.

l: the Hour, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: When the Hour rises, the unrighteous will despair, people will be sundered, and the guilty will realize that their excuses and attempted amends will not benefit them.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: The Day of Resurrection is the appointed day when people will be separated and their worldly claims will be exposed. Those given knowledge and faith affirm that people remained until it by Allah's decree.

l: creation, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Allah produces creation, then reproduces it, and returning creation to Him is easier for Him. He created mankind from dust and shaped people through weakness, strength, weakness, and grey hair.

l: resurrection, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Resurrection is shown through Allah bringing the living from the dead, the dead from the living, and reviving the earth after its death. People will be brought forth from the earth and given life again.

l: Allah's promise, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Allah's promise is true and cannot fail. Muhammad is told to remain patient because Allah's promise will come to pass.

l: Allah's help to victory, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Allah helps to victory whom He wills. Believers will rejoice in Allah's help to victory when the Romans become victorious after their defeat.

l: the Qur'an, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: The Qur'an contains all kinds of similitudes for mankind. Those who disbelieve may call its messenger a trickster when shown a miracle.

l: Allah's revelations, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Allah's revelations are denied and mocked by disbelievers. They are presented as guidance, and Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know.

l: Allah's signs, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Allah's signs include human creation, spouses and love, differences of languages and colours, sleep, provision, lightning, rain, the heavens and the earth, and resurrection. They are portents for people who reflect, have knowledge, heed, understand, or believe.

l: religion, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: The upright religion is to turn to Allah, follow the nature in which He created mankind, be mindful of duty to Him, establish worship, and avoid partners. People are warned not to split up their religion into sects.

l: Allah's mercy, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Allah's mercy is seen in rain that revives the earth and in winds that herald it. People rejoice when they taste His mercy, although some then attribute partners to their Lord.

l: usury, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: What people give in usury to increase another person's property has no increase with Allah.

l: charity, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: What people give in charity while seeking Allah's Countenance has increase manifold. Giving to relatives, the needy, and the wayfarer is described as best for those who seek Allah's Countenance.

l: corruption, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Corruption appears on land and sea because of what people's hands have done. Allah makes them taste part of what they have done so that they may return.

l: partners ascribed to Allah, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: People who ascribe partners to Allah reject His gifts and follow their own lusts without knowledge. Their partners cannot intercede for them on the day of the Hour, and Allah is exalted above what they associate with Him.

l: the meeting with their Lord, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Many of mankind disbelieve in the meeting with their Lord. Those who deny the meeting of the Hereafter are condemned to doom.

l: the splitting of religion, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: Those who split up their religion become schismatics, with each sect exulting in its own tenets. They are included among those warned against associating partners with Allah.

l: the nature of Allah, Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room), Surah 30: The Romans (Ar-Room)
s: The nature of Allah is the nature in which He created mankind. There is no altering Allah's creation, and following this nature is identified with the right religion.

l: Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Surah 31, Luqman, concerns guidance, faith, worship, gratitude, and the consequences of belief or disbelief. Allah describes the wise Scripture, the creation of the heavens and the earth, and signs showing His power and wisdom. Luqman is given wisdom and instructs his son to avoid associating partners with Allah, honor parents, establish worship, enjoin kindness, forbid iniquity, persevere, and remain humble. The unit warns mankind about the Hereafter, the life of the world, the Day of judgment, and matters known only to Allah.

l: Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman), Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Surah 31 is called Luqman and is revealed at Mecca. It presents guidance, warnings, signs of Allah, and Luqman's counsel to his son.

l: Allah, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Allah is described as the Absolute, the Owner of Praise, the Mighty, the Wise, the Hearer, the Knower, the Sublime, and the Aware. Allah created the heavens and the earth, provides guidance and mercy, controls the night, day, sun, moon, rain, and resurrection, and knows the unseen.

l: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Luqman is given wisdom and tells his son to give thanks to Allah, avoid associating partners with Him, establish worship, enjoin kindness, forbid iniquity, persevere, and behave humbly.

l: the wise Scripture, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: The wise Scripture contains revelations that are a guidance and a mercy for the good.

l: revelations, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: The revelations are recited to people, but some turn away from them in pride and mockery. Those who heed them receive guidance, while those who reject them face painful or shameful doom.

l: those who establish worship and pay the poor-due, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Those who establish worship, pay the poor-due, and have sure faith in the Hereafter receive guidance from their Lord and are successful.

l: mankind, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Mankind includes believers, disbelievers, those who dispute about Allah without knowledge, and those who follow inherited practices even when the devil invites them to the doom of flame. Mankind is warned to keep duty to Allah and not be deceived by worldly life.

l: the gardens of delight, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: The gardens of delight are prepared for those who believe and do good works. They will abide therein as a true promise from Allah.

l: the heavens, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: The heavens were created without visible supports. Allah owns what is in the heavens and uses them among the signs of His power.

l: the earth, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: The earth contains firm hills, beasts, and plants brought forth by water from the sky. Allah owns what is in the earth, and even if its trees became pens, its words could not be exhausted.

l: Creation of Allah, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Creation of Allah includes the heavens, the earth, hills, beasts, plants, and all that Allah has made serviceable to mankind. Those worshipped beside Allah have created nothing.

l: wisdom, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Wisdom was given to Luqman, who used it to teach gratitude to Allah and proper conduct toward Allah, parents, and other people.

l: Luqman's son, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Luqman's son is addressed with repeated counsel. He is told to reject partners unto Allah, honor his parents without obeying them in disbelief, establish worship, enjoin kindness, forbid iniquity, persevere, avoid arrogance, and lower his voice.

l: partners unto Allah, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Ascribing partners unto Allah is described as a tremendous wrong. Luqman's son is told not to obey parents if they strive to make him ascribe partners to Allah, while still treating them kindly in the world.

l: worship, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Worship is to be established, and those who establish it along with paying the poor-due and believing in the Hereafter are guided and successful. Allah alone is to be worshipped and thanked.

l: the devil, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: The devil may invite people to follow inherited practices that lead to the doom of flame. People are warned not to let the deceiver beguile them regarding Allah.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: The Hereafter is believed in with sure faith by the successful. Allah warns that people will return to Him and that the parent and child will not be able to avail one another on the Day.

l: the signs of Allah, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: The signs of Allah include the creation of the heavens and earth, the movement of night and day, the sun and moon, ships on the sea, and the raising of the dead. None denies these signs except every traitor ingrate.

l: the Day, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: The Day is a promised reality when the parent cannot avail the child and the child cannot avail the parent. The life of the world must not deceive people about it.

l: the life of the world, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: The life of the world is temporary and must not beguile people. Allah gives disbelievers comfort for a little before driving them to a heavy doom.

l: the Hour, Surah 31: Luqman, Surah 31: Luqman (Luqman)
s: Knowledge of the Hour belongs with Allah. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or in what land it will die.

l: Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), revealed at Mecca, concerns the truth of the Scripture and Allah’s creation, guidance, and judgment. It warns the people addressed by Muhammad about resurrection, punishment, and the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing. It describes believers who prostrate, pray, spend from what they have been given, and receive the Gardens of Retreat, while evildoers face the Fire. The unit also recounts Moses, the Scripture given to him, the Children of Israel, and Allah’s judgment on the Day of Resurrection.

l: Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda) was revealed at Mecca. It presents warnings about disbelief, resurrection, punishment, and judgment, along with guidance for believers.

l: Allah, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: Allah created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six Days, mounted the Throne, and directs the ordinance from heaven to earth. Allah created humanity, fashioned people, breathed into them of His Spirit, and appointed hearing, sight, and hearts for them.

l: the Scripture, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: The Scripture is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds, without doubt. Allah gave the Scripture to Moses as guidance for the Children of Israel.

l: the Lord of the Worlds, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: The Lord of the Worlds is identified as the source of the revelation of the Scripture.

l: the people warned by Muhammad, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: The people warned by Muhammad are a folk to whom no warner came before him. They are warned so that they may walk aright.

l: the angel of death, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: The angel of death has charge concerning people and will gather them. Afterward, they will be returned unto their Lord.

l: the guilty, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: The guilty will hang their heads before their Lord and ask to be sent back so they can do right. Allah says that the guilty will be requited.

l: mankind, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: Mankind is included with the jinn among those whom Allah will fill hell with if they are evildoers. Mankind will be returned unto the Lord after death.

l: hell, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: Hell will be filled with the jinn and mankind together because of evildoing.

l: the meeting with their Lord, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: Disbelievers deny the meeting with their Lord. The guilty will recognize it when they are brought before their Lord and ask to return.

l: the doom of immortality, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: The doom of immortality is tasted because of what people used to do and because they forgot the meeting of their day.

l: believers, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: Believers in Allah’s revelations fall down prostrate when reminded of them, hymn the praise of their Lord, forsake their beds to pray in fear and hope, and spend from what they have been given. They are promised the Gardens of Retreat for their belief and good works.

l: the Gardens of Retreat, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: The Gardens of Retreat are the welcome and reward for those who believe and do good works.

l: the Fire, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: The Fire is the retreat of those who do evil. When they desire to leave it, they are brought back and told to taste the torment they used to deny.

l: the revelations of Allah, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: Allah’s revelations are believed by those who prostrate when reminded of them and are not scornful. Those who turn away after being reminded of them are described as guilty.

l: Moses, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: Moses was given the Scripture, which Allah appointed as a guidance for the Children of Israel.

l: the Children of Israel, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: The Children of Israel received the Scripture given to Moses. When they became steadfast and believed firmly in Allah’s revelations, leaders were appointed from among them to guide by Allah’s command.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: On the Day of Resurrection, the Lord will judge between people concerning that wherein they used to differ.

l: Muhammad, Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda), Surah 32: The Prostration (As-Sajda)
s: Muhammad is told to warn the people to whom no warner came before him. He is also told to withdraw from those who disbelieve and await the event.

l: Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab), Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab), Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab)
s: This unit concerns Allah's guidance to Muhammad, the Prophet, and the believers, including conduct, faith, obedience, remembrance, and trust. It recounts the clans' attack, the believers' trial and steadfastness, Allah's aid, and the defeat of the disbelievers. It gives instructions concerning the Prophet's wives, the household, marriage, modesty, and relations with the Prophet. It warns hypocrites, disbelievers, and those who malign Allah, His messenger, or believing men and women, and describes the Hour, the Hereafter, reward, and punishment.

l: Allah, Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab), Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab)
s: Allah is described as Knower, Wise, Aware, Forgiving, Merciful, Strong, Mighty, and Able to do all things. Allah guides, protects, tests, rewards, forgives, punishes, and has prepared the Hereafter's reward and punishment. Allah sent wind and unseen hosts against the clans, repulsed the disbelievers, and brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them.

s: Muhammad is identified as the messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. He is closer to the believers than their selves, is sent as a witness, bearer of good tidings, warner, summoner unto Allah, and a lamp that gives light. He is instructed to obey Allah, trust Him, remember Him, and convey guidance.

s: The believers are instructed to obey Allah and His messenger, remember and glorify Allah, speak straight words, guard their duty, and follow the Prophet's example. During the clans' attack they were sorely tried, while the true believers recognized Allah's and His messenger's promise and increased in faith and resignation. Allah promises believing men and women forgiveness and a vast reward.

l: hypocrites, Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab), Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab)
s: The hypocrites are warned against obeying or supporting them, and they are described as doubting Allah's and His messenger's promises, hindering the believers, fleeing from battle, and showing fear and greed. Allah makes their deeds fruitless, curses them if they persist in spreading alarm, and prepares punishment for them.

l: disbelievers, Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab), Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab)
s: The disbelievers and their allies advanced against the believers with the clans but gained no good. Allah repulsed them in their wrath and prepared a flaming fire for those who disbelieve, where they will abide forever without a protecting friend or helper.

l: the Prophet's wives, Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab), Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab)
s: The Prophet's wives are described as mothers of the believers and are given instructions concerning modesty, speech, residence, prayer, almsgiving, obedience, and remembrance of revelation and wisdom. They may choose Allah, His messenger, and the abode of the Hereafter with an immense reward, or receive worldly provision and a fair release. The text also gives rules concerning their conduct, relatives, access to their dwellings, and interaction from behind a curtain.

l: the clans, Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab), Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab)
s: The clans came against the believers from above and below, causing fear and a severe trial. Allah sent against them a great wind and unseen hosts, and later repulsed them so that they gained no good.

l: the Hour, Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab), Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab)
s: Men ask Muhammad about the Hour. He is instructed to say that knowledge of it belongs only to Allah and that it may be near.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab), Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab)
s: The Hereafter is presented as the abode desired by those who choose Allah and His messenger over worldly life. The faithful are promised forgiveness, a vast reward, peace, and goodly recompense, while disbelievers and those who disobey are threatened with lasting punishment.

l: the Battle of the Clans, Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab), Surah 33: The Clans (Al-Ahzaab)
s: The Battle of the Clans is described as a time when hosts came against the believers, who were frightened, tested, and shaken. Allah aided the believers with wind and unseen hosts, exposed the hypocrites, repulsed the disbelievers, and granted the believers victory and spoils.

s: This unit concerns the Qur'an's warning to disbelievers and recounts the fate of earlier peoples who denied messengers. It describes Allah's gifts, trials, forgiveness, and judgments involving David, Solomon, Job, and other chosen servants. It contrasts believers and the righteous with transgressors, describing Gardens of Eden for the former and the Fire and Hell for the latter. It recounts the angels' prostration before the created mortal, Iblis's refusal and punishment, and the warning that all peoples will come to know the truth.

l: Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: It is revealed at Mecca and begins by invoking the renowned Qur'an. It warns of disbelievers' pride and schism and ends by declaring that its truth will become known.

l: Allah, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: Allah is described as One, the Mighty, the Bestower, the Pardoning, and the Absolute. Allah destroys denying peoples, tests and forgives servants, grants sovereignty and gifts, and will fill Hell with Iblis and those who follow him.

l: the Qur'an, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The Qur'an is renowned and is invoked as evidence against those who deny. Its revelation is presented as a warning and a reminder.

l: disbelievers, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: Disbelievers reject the warner, call him a wizard and charlatan, object to worshipping One Allah, and claim the message is an invention. They are warned of doom, the Fire, and Hell.

l: warner, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The warner comes from among the people and is rejected by disbelievers. He is sent to give a plain warning and asks no fee.

l: Muhammad, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: Muhammad is addressed as the one who is to say that he is only a warner, that there is no Allah save Allah, and that he asks no fee. He is told to bear what people say and to recount the warnings and examples in the revelation.

l: the earth, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The earth and all that is between it and the heavens were not created in vain. Allah sets David as a viceroy in the earth and warns against spreading corruption in it.

l: the Day of Reckoning, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The Day of Reckoning is the day before which disbelievers ask that their fate be hastened. It is forgotten by those who wander from the way of Allah, and the promised provision of the righteous is for that day.

l: David, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: David is described as a bondman of might who continually turned in repentance. Allah strengthened his kingdom, gave him wisdom and decisive speech, subdued the hills and birds to hymn praises with him, tested him through the litigants, forgave him, and appointed him a viceroy in the earth.

l: the litigants, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The litigants climbed the wall into David's royal chamber and frightened him before assuring him they sought a judgment. One claimed that the other, who had ninety-nine ewes, demanded his single ewe and overcame him in speech.

l: the way of Allah, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: David is commanded to judge rightly and not follow desire away from the way of Allah. Those who wander from the way of Allah face an awful doom because they forgot the Day of Reckoning.

l: the Fire, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The Fire is the fate threatened to those who disbelieve and spread corruption. Its torment includes boiling and ice-cold draughts and other paired extremes.

l: believers, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: Believers who do good works are distinguished from those who spread corruption. They are associated with the pious and with the promised reward of Gardens of Eden.

l: the Scripture, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The Scripture is revealed unto Muhammad full of blessing. Its purpose is that people ponder its revelations and that men of understanding reflect.

l: Solomon, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: Solomon is given as an excellent slave who continually turned in repentance. Allah tried him, accepted his repentance, granted his request for sovereignty, and made the wind, builders, divers, and others subservient to him.

l: Job, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: Job cries to his Lord that the devil afflicts him with distress and torment. Allah directs him to strike the ground, restores his household and the like thereof, and describes him as steadfast and continually repentant.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The Hereafter is called the Home whose remembrance purified Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The chosen servants are associated with remembrance of this Home.

l: the righteous, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The righteous are promised a happy journey's end, Gardens of Eden, abundant fruit, cool drink, and companions of modest gaze. Their provision will never waste away.

l: Gardens of Eden, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: Gardens of Eden are promised to those who ward off evil. Their gates are opened for them, and they recline there with plenteous fruit, cool drink, and companions.

l: Hell, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: Hell is the destination of Iblis and those who follow him. Its dwellers argue, blame their misleaders, ask for double portions of the Fire for those who led them astray, and burn in an evil resting-place.

l: the reminder, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The reminder is disputed by disbelievers, who are said not yet to have tasted Allah's doom. It is also presented as a revealed blessing for reflection and as a reminder for all peoples.

l: the angels, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The angels are commanded to fall prostrate before the mortal fashioned by Allah. They all prostrate, except Iblis.

l: Iblis, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: Iblis refuses to prostrate, claiming superiority because he was created from fire while the mortal was created from clay. He is cast out, cursed until the Day of Judgment, reprieved until the appointed time, and declares that he will beguile everyone except Allah's single-minded slaves.

l: all peoples, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)

l: the truth, Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad), Surah 38: The letter Saad (Saad)
s: The truth is declared to be tremendous tidings from which people turn away. It is spoken by Allah and will become known in time.

It describes Allah's power over the heavens, the earth, human beings, life, death, and the soul, and recounts the events of the Day of Resurrection. It concludes with disbelievers entering hell and those who keep their duty to Allah entering the Garden.

l: Allah, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Allah reveals the Scripture with truth, commands worship, judges between people, guides whom He wills, and forgives those who repent. l: Muhammad, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)

l: the Scripture, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)

l: revelation, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)

l: pure religion, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)

l: believers, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)

l: disbelievers, Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar), Surah 39: The Groups (Az-Zumar)
s: Disbelievers reject truth, prefer false gods, and are warned of humiliation and everlasting doom. On the Day of Resurrection they are driven to hell in troops.
